title: Solving a Rubik's cube
examples: What is the easiest way to start solving a Rubik's cube?
Do I need to memorize a lot of moves?
How many steps does the beginner method take?

explain.say: The Rubik's cube has six colored faces. Each face has a different color to help you see.

items: Center piece: Defines the face color
Edge pieces: Two colors on one side
Corner pieces: Three colors meet here

explain.say: We solve the cube in layers, starting from the first layer on one side. This builds a solid base.

draw.text: Layers: Build from the base up

explain.say: Algorithms are specific sequences of turns. You must follow these exact steps to move pieces correctly.
The beginner method starts by completing the first face and the first layer. This gives you a stable base.

items: When: First Layer: Build the base
When: Second Layer: Place edge pieces
When: Third Layer: Orient last pieces

explain.say: For a real-life example, think about stacking colored blocks. You must build them layer by layer to make a tower.

items: Middle layer: Blocks stacked on top
Top layer: The final piece placed

explain.say: A common mistake is guessing the turns instead of using the algorithm. Always check your instructions first.

faq.q: Do I need to learn all the algorithms at once?
faq.a: No, you learn them in small groups as you progress through the layers. You only need the ones for the current step.
asks: What is the order of learning moves?
Is it hard to remember all the moves?

faq.q: What is the difference between a face and a layer?
faq.a: A face is one of the six visible sides, like the blue side. A layer is a horizontal slice of pieces you turn at a time.
asks: Are faces and layers the same thing?
How many layers are there in total?

faq.q: Can I solve the cube without knowing any algorithms?
faq.a: You can try, but it will be very difficult and slow. Algorithms give you a reliable path to success.
asks: Is it possible to solve it by feel?
What is the absolute first thing I should learn?

faq.q: What should I focus on when I start learning?
faq.a: Focus first on getting the entire first face solved, and then matching the edge pieces on the first layer.
asks: Where should I begin my practice?
What is the easiest part to master first?

faq.q: Does the beginner method work for all cubes?
faq.a: The beginner method is designed for the standard 3x3x3 cube. It is a great starting point for everyone.
asks: Is this method only for beginners?
Does this technique work on different sized cubes?

facts: The standard cube has six faces, each with a unique color.
Solving involves working in distinct layers, building from the bottom up.
Algorithms are precise, repeatable sequences of turns.
The beginner method breaks the complex puzzle into manageable steps.

quiz.say: If you are solving the second layer, what are you primarily trying to match?
quiz.show: Matching edges to the side colors.

options.show: Corner pieces must match the center.
options.say: Corner pieces must match the center.

options.show: You should only worry about the top face.
options.say: You should only worry about the top face.

options.show: You can just turn pieces until they look right.
options.say: You can just turn pieces until they look right.

options.show: Edge pieces must match the side colors.
options.say: Edge pieces must match the side colors.

quiz.why: The second layer pieces must align with the center colors of the sides.

wrong.0: Corner pieces are usually solved in the final layer, not the second.
wrong.1: Solving requires working systematically across all visible faces.
wrong.2: Guessing turns is unreliable; algorithms provide the correct sequence.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of using algorithms?

options.show: You can change the turns if it feels better.
options.say: You can change the turns if it feels better.

options.show: Algorithms provide the exact sequence of turns needed.
options.say: Algorithms provide the exact sequence of turns needed.

options.show: They are just suggestions for turning pieces.
options.say: They are just suggestions for turning pieces.

options.show: They only help with the last layer.
options.say: They only help with the last layer.

quiz.why: Algorithms remove guesswork by giving you a proven, step-by-step solution.

wrong.0: Changing turns breaks the mathematical sequence required for the puzzle.
wrong.2: They are not suggestions; they are mandatory, precise instructions.
wrong.3: Algorithms are used across multiple layers, not just the final one.

quiz.say: When solving the cube, which process is best described as building a stable base?

options.show: Focusing only on the center piece.
options.say: Focusing only on the center piece.

quiz.why: Starting with the first layer creates a solid foundation for all subsequent steps.

wrong.0: The center is important, but you must solve the pieces around it too.
wrong.1: This method has no structure and will not lead to a solution.
wrong.3: This is too complex; you need a base to build upon.
